subject.title: Remote gateway node pairing broken — node token scopes empty, approval flow incomplete

question: What remote-node trust contract should OpenClaw enforce between device role approval, node capability approval, node-token scopes, and node-role rotation for external gateways?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans Windows UX and gateway authorization, and a wrong default could either keep users stuck at zero capabilities or broaden remote command execution authority.

options.title: Keep split trust and improve recovery
options.body: Preserve explicit node capability approval, then make the Windows tray and CLI show the pending node request, safe approval command, and token-drift recovery state clearly.

options.title: Bridge role approval to node trust
options.body: Let device role approval grant or guide node capability trust more aggressively, but require a gateway security review and live remote proof before landing.

options.title: Defer Windows changes until gateway contract lands
options.body: Keep this issue open but block client work until the gateway-side issue defines token scopes, request ID namespaces, and node-role rotation behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep split trust and improve recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve explicit node capability approval, then make the Windows tray and CLI show the pending node request, safe approval command, and token-drift recovery state clearly.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged Windows-client partial fix and explicitly documented which remote/gateway-side behaviors remained unresolved.
